trust_decision.summary: Before an integration webhook is dialled, the target must be resolved and accepted only if it is a public http(s) address, that validated address must be pinned for the actual TCP connection, 30x redirects must not be followed, and the only exceptions are an operator allowlist (exact hosts/suffixes) or allowPrivateUrlInIntegration. The decision belongs at the shared outbound primitive Addon.fetchRetry (src/lib/addons/addon.ts), which every request-sending provider reaches, with an earlier copy of the same decision in AddonService.createAddon/updateAddon so a bad URL is refused at configuration time as well.

landing_point.why: The summary says the addon webhook URL is dialled server-side with no internal-address filtering; this is the only outbound HTTP call in the integrations path (ky(url, ...)), shared by webhook, slack, teams, teams-workflow, datadog and new-relic, and its options are typed any and spread after retry, so a reader lands here as the single place to guard.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The config builder is not the dialler: the advisory is about outbound fetches, so a solver can argue that an operator-level private-URL switch is a feature/ops concern that belongs to whoever complained, not to the URL check, and that no change is needed there.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Updating an existing integration without re-entering the URL: for slack, teams, teams-workflow, webhook and new-relic the url parameter is sensitive:true, so the config API returns '*****' and the update handler restores the stored value. An unconditional URL check rejects every such update, and a blanket private-IP block also breaks the legitimate self-hosted case of an integration pointed at an internal host, which the fix preserves through allowPrivateUrlInIntegration / allowListIntegration.

O6_input_shapes: scheme variants: non-http(s) URL (e.g. file:///etc/passwd) rejected before any request is made
literal IPv4 address in the URL, taken through the net.isIP branch with no DNS lookup
literal IPv6 and IPv4-mapped IPv6 (::ffff:0:0/96) checked against the v4 and v6 private/reserved subnets
hostname resolving to several A/AAAA records: every answer is checked and the first is pinned
hostname whose DNS answer changes between validation and connect (rebinding): the connection uses the pinned address, lookup is called once
30x response whose Location points at a metadata/internal host (redirect: 'manual', the 302 is returned rather than followed)
update request that sends back the masked value '*****' for the sensitive url parameter (check skipped, stored value kept)
allowlisted host or allowlisted suffix (private target permitted only by operator configuration)
